continuity.arc_goal: Implement Promise Objects API with compile-time type safety for linked workflows in the Rust SDK, replacing runtime-heavy approach with design-time validation

progress_update.summary: Massive session — designed and implemented the Promise Objects API for the Rust SDK. Started with design discussion (StartRequest, #[start], PromiseContextT, WorkflowContextT), then executed 4-phase implementation. Post-implementation, refactored Invocation to Invocation<T> with phantom result type, removed Cancellation, moved result-awaiting to WorkflowContextT::get_output(), and wired ctx.resolve() to the real sys_resolve syscall from sdk-shared-core. All 40 tests passing.
progress_update.goal: Implement Promise Objects API with compile-time type safety for the Restate Rust SDK
accomplished: Designed Promise Objects API: StartRequest (renamed from RunRequest), #[start] attribute, PromiseContextT, WorkflowContextT, ContextResolve trait
Implemented all 4 phases: rename, macro parsing, new context types, generator updates, compile tests
Refactored Invocation to Invocation<T> with PhantomData<fn() -> T> — carries result type, no Send/static bounds needed
Removed Cancellation type entirely — Invocation<T> is the single handle type with id() and cancel()
Added WorkflowContextT::get_output(&inv) — only workflow contexts can await linked child results, returns DurableFuture
Wired ctx.resolve() and ctx.resolve_failure() to real sys_resolve syscall (no more todo!() stubs)
Code review completed — H1 (StartRequestT return type) and H2 (test coverage) findings fixed
progress_update.now: Implementation complete. All 40 tests passing. 18 uncommitted files. Ready for commit/cleanup.
next_steps: Update the design doc to reflect final API (Invocation<T>, get_output, no Cancellation)
Consider squashing commits for clean PR history
Switch shared-core from path dep back to published version before PR
constraints: No E2E integration test harness — SDK→shared-core VM tested, wire protocol→server tested separately
decisions: StartRequest replaces RunRequest (rename, not new type). #[start] on non-shared Object/Workflow handlers controls which client methods return StartRequest
Invocation<T> with PhantomData<fn() -> T> — no Send/'static bounds on T. Cancellation removed entirely
get_output(&inv) on WorkflowContextT only — result-awaiting is a context capability, not on the handle
PromiseContextT is a new struct (not type alias) — unconditionally implements SealedCanResolve
Linking gated to T-suffix contexts only (ObjectContextT, PromiseContextT, WorkflowContextT)
Promise Objects API supersedes prior Invocation/Cancellation design from sessions 5-7
open_questions: Should RunRequest be kept as a type alias for backward compat?
Should #[start] be required on at least one handler for PromiseContextT objects?
risks: Three repos need coordinated branches for PR (sdk-rust, sdk-shared-core, restate server)
No E2E wire protocol test — integration only verified at VM and server levels separately
Large API redesign may need extensive documentation updates for clarity
